div.head: II Cn 55
div.ab: Ælþeodige men, gif hig heora hæmed rihtan nellan, of lande mid heora æhtum ⁊ synnan gewitan.
Ælðeodige men, gif hig heora hemed rihtan nellað, [driuc hi man of] lande mid heora æhtan ⁊ on synnan gewitan.
Ælþeodige menn, gif hig heora hæmed rihtan nillan, of lande mid heora æhtum ⁊ synnan gewitan.
Alienigenę si concubitus suos dirigere nolint, extra patriam cum pecunia et peccatis recedant.
Alieni nisi legale coniugium custodierint, expellantur de terra cum substantia et peccatis.
[55] Alienigene qui suam uenerem corrigere neggligunt, a patria cum sua substantia et peccato discedant.
Ælðeodige men, gif hig heora hemed rihtan nellað, [driue hi man of] lande mid heora æhtan ⁊ on synnan gewitan.
Ælþeodige men, gif hig heora hæmed rihtan nellan, driue hi man of lande mid heora æhtum and synnan gewitan.
Fremde Männer, wenn sie ihren Geschlechtsverkehr nicht rechtmässig machen wollen, sollen (treibe man sie B) aus dem Lande mit ihren Gütern und (in B) Sünden weichen.
Foreign men, if they will not make their sexual relations lawful, shall depart (let them be driven, B) from the land with their goods and (in, B) sins.
Foreigners, if they will not regularise their unions, shall be driven from the land with their possessions, and shall depart in sin.
Foreigners, if they will not regularise their marriages, are to depart from the land with their goods and their sins.
If foreigners will not make their marriages conform to the law, they shall be expelled from the realm with their possessions and leave with their sins.

note.seg: Written in the margin in 16th cent. in B; om. G, A, Ld.
This clause is taken unchanged from the laws of the Kentish king, Wihtred (4). It is probably the influx of Scandinavians in the reign of Cnut that caused the revival of this ancient statute.
